Hey! Listen! Nintendo’s Ocarina Of Time Remake Fully Revealed

By
Peter Paltridge
-
September 8, 2026
84
0

WhatsApp

    Sponsored by

    Today was the day Nintendo finally let us see what this fall’s anticipated Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 looks like. Until this morning, all we’ve had to go on is one shot of Link sleeping and the logo. No one knew what kind of remake this was…a faithful one-to-one reimagining of the environments, or a dramatically reinvented open world game bringing the 1998 classic closer to Breath of the Wild?

    Now we know it’s going to be the former. Today’s Direct revealed a lot more of the game than we figured it would; there was at least one clip from every dungeon and area except Ganon’s Castle in the presentation. It looks to be the same game, and series producer Eiji Aonuma proved it by playing one uninterrupted string of gameplay from Kokiri Forest to the first few rooms of the Deku Tree. You had to laugh at Aonuma carefully explaining how to obtain the Fairy Slingshot as if we all haven’t done this a million times before.

    Yet while the game is mostly the same experience, the visuals are VASTLY different, especially Kokiri Forest, the first area we were allowed to see. In a sense, this is the game you played in your mind back in the 90s, when your imagination had to fill the details in the smeary textures and blocky areas. I would say this should put an end to the “Hire this man” jokes on social media, but since it is impossible to please everybody, and algorithms boost negative comments over positive ones, no…the Internet would never be pleased by this game no matter what it looked like.

    There are some new additions if you know where to look. Modern conveniences like a freely adjustable camera, menu-less item switching and a quest tracker were all expected, but Link can now also jump, an ability no previous version of Ocarina of Time ever had. He can also dash if you hold down the A button, and wow, we needed that in 1998. Cutscenes will be fully voiced, something I know some fans were demanding but may regret. We now have confirmation I’ve been pronouncing Saria’s name wrong.

    Nintendo’s online store will soon stock a real ocarina, and you can even use it in the game. A microphone feature will let you hum the magical songs, and it’ll pick up the ocarina notes. Other real-world items will soon include Young Link and Young Zelda amiibos (in 2027), new Zelda Lego sets and a special edition of the Switch 2 with OOT-inspired designs on the console, controller and stand.

    Despite the stream being billed as about the 40th anniversary of the series as a whole, there wasn’t a lot that wasn’t about this one game, but there was some fresh news on the movie. They’re calling it “The Legend Of Zelda” — big shock, right? But Miyamoto says once we see the film, “we’ll know why it has no subtitle.” Perhaps it’s Zelda who saves the day in the end, not Link.

    The new Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will be released for Nintendo Switch 2 November 5. Preorders are open now, with the physical edition costing ten bucks more ($59.99 digital, $69.99 physical).
